description: Advanced Encryption Standard - High-speed symmetric block cipher utilizing 128, 192, or 256-bit key sizes.
Data Encryption Standard - Legacy 56-bit symmetric block cipher now deemed insecure due to short key length.
Triple Data Encryption Standard - Legacy symmetric encryption applying DES algorithm three times per data block.
Rivest-Shamir-Adleman - Asymmetric encryption algorithm based on the mathematical difficulty of factoring large prime numbers.
Elliptic Curve Cryptography - Efficient asymmetric cryptography providing high security using small key lengths.
Diffie-Hellman - Key exchange algorithm allowing two parties to establish a shared secret key over an insecure channel.
Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman - Key exchange algorithm combining Diffie-Hellman logic with elliptic curve cryptography.
Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm - Asymmetric algorithm utilizing ECC mathematics to create digital signatures.
Secure Hash Algorithm - Family of cryptographic hash functions generating fixed-size mathematical digests.
Secure Hash Algorithm 1 - Deprecated 160-bit hash function susceptible to collision attacks.
Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit - Secure hash function producing a 256-bit digest value.
Secure Hash Algorithm 384-bit - Strong variant of SHA-2 generating 384-bit output digests.
Secure Hash Algorithm 512-bit - High-security hash function producing 512-bit digest outputs.
Message Digest 5 - Legacy 128-bit hashing algorithm vulnerable to collision attacks; unfit for modern security.
Hash-Based Message Authentication Code - Integrity checksum combining a hash function with a secret key.
Public Key Infrastructure - Complete ecosystem managing digital certificates and asymmetric key pairs.
Certificate Authority - Trusted third-party entity issuing and verifying digital X.509 identity certificates.
Certificate Revocation List - Published list of revoked digital certificates updated periodically by a CA.
Online Certificate Status Protocol - Real-time query mechanism for validating digital certificate revocation status.
Certificate Signing Request - Encrypted message sent to a Certificate Authority requesting a new digital certificate.
Distinguished Encoding Rules - Binary encoding format used for X.509 digital certificates and key files.
Privacy-Enhanced Mail - ASCII Base64 encoded file format used for storing certificates and private keys.
Pretty Good Privacy - Encryption program providing cryptographic privacy and data authentication for email files.
GNU Privacy Guard - Free open-source implementation of the OpenPGP encryption standard.
Transport Layer Security - Modern cryptographic protocol securing data in transit over computer networks.
Secure Sockets Layer - Deprecated predecessor to TLS; vulnerable to fallback attacks.
Datagram Transport Layer Security - Protocol adapting TLS capabilities for UDP connectionless communications.
Internet Key Exchange - Protocol used to set up Security Associations and shared keys in IPsec VPN tunnels.
Internet Protocol Security - Protocol suite securing IP layer data using authentication and encryption features.
Authentication Header - IPsec protocol providing data integrity and authentication without data encryption.
Encapsulating Security Payload - IPsec protocol providing data confidentiality, authentication, and integrity.
Pre-Shared Key - Secret cryptographic key shared out-of-band between communicating parties prior to session setup.
Key Management System - System managing creation, storage, distribution, and destruction of cryptographic keys.
Temporal Key Integrity Protocol - Legacy WPA encryption protocol developed to temporarily fix WEP weaknesses.
Counter Mode/CBC-MAC Protocol - AES-based encryption protocol implemented in WPA2 wireless security.
